column3: Near-identical formulation joins fabrication against Allah, denial of truth on its arrival, and Hell as the disbelievers' abode.
Crisis-born devotion followed by withdrawal offers a secondary instance of gratitude reversed into disbelief.
It develops the focus's abode consequence as a permanent entry into Hell for the arrogant.
Its formula names fabrication against Allah and denial of His signs as the gravest injustice, adding the failure of wrongdoers.
The local declaration of death and return gives a limited horizon for the accountability in the focus.
It confirms that the Fire is a fixed abode once repentance can no longer alter the outcome.
It closely repeats fabrication against Allah and denial of His signs, with the added verdict that criminals do not prosper.
Their confession that Allah created all things, followed by their deviation, supplies local context for their false allegiance.
The accusation that revelation was fabricated is directly answered by its being truth from the Lord.
It joins lying against Allah to visible shame and Hell as the arrogant person's abode.
The local turn to disbelief after benefit received is a proximate but less specific form of the focus's denial.
It shows a historical pattern of messengers being denied after clear proofs and illuminating scripture arrived.
It repeats fabrication against Allah and adds public witnessing and curse at final presentation.

It names severe punishment for disbelievers but adds little beyond the established consequence.
Their sincere call in peril followed by association after rescue gives the nearest local enactment of faith reversed.
The description of ritual mockery is too indirect to illuminate the focus's central relation.
The unavoidable punishment for disbelievers generally supports the focus's consequence.
It introduces their false speech, a broad antecedent to fabricating a lie about Allah.
It contrasts truth from the Lord with chosen disbelief and gives a vivid enclosing Fire consequence.
It condenses denial and turning away, but contributes no new account of truth's arrival or fabrication.
Provision's expansion and restriction do not clarify the focus's accusation or judgment.
Rejecting the requested reminder when it arrives is a secondary parallel to denial of truth received.
At the Fire, former deniers must affirm that the warned reality was true before tasting punishment.
The local contrast between worldly play and real final life frames the seriousness of the focus's outcome.
It directly shows clear verses and truth on arrival being dismissed as manifest magic.
The disbelievers' compelled confession that this is truth immediately precedes punishment for their disbelief.
Human honor across land and sea does not clarify the focus's falsehood or final abode.
Disbelief and obstructing God's way causing deeds to fail is a broad consequence parallel.

Scripture sent with truth and confirming prior revelation clarifies the divine source opposed by fabrication claims.
The Pharaoh household's taking of Moses has no focused relation to the verse.
Disbelief in Allah and His messenger explains rejected deeds, a secondary consequence of the focus's disbelief.

The fabrication accusation is answered by a challenge to produce comparable fabricated chapters.
The Lot narrative scene does not add a focused connection to the verse.
The declaration of God's knowledge and mercy does not clarify the focus's accusation or judgment.

The mirage portrays disbelieving works as false appearance exposed at encounter with Allah and full reckoning.
The believers' garden reward is too general after the local positive abode has already appeared.

Its dismissal of a promise does not identify truth's arrival, fabrication, or an abode consequence.

Believers know the Hour is true while its disputants are far astray, a secondary truth-denial contrast.
Divine effective will alone does not clarify the focus's relations.
Persistent evil culminates in denial and mockery of God's signs, adding a behavioral pathway to the focus.
Wonder at the arrival of a human warner begins a related but less specific rejection pattern.

Calling on an unproven deity and failing to prosper offers a secondary false-allegiance parallel.

It identifies the claim that Allah has begotten as a lie, a concrete form of fabrication about Allah.
It declares the arrival of truth and the incapacity of falsehood to originate or restore anything.
After truth has been established, fabricating a lie against Allah is again named wrongdoing.
The rhetorical challenge to the false offspring allocation supplies limited context for fabrication about Allah.
It condenses the paired actions of denial and turning away without the focus's arriving-truth or abode elements.

Creation and possible gathering do not add a specific link to fabrication or denial of truth.
It warns that selective rejection of God, messengers, books, and the Last Day is far error.
It explicitly records a people dismissing their messenger as one who fabricated a lie against Allah.
The recurring woe for deniers reinforces judgment but is marginal after fuller consequence verses.
It directly contrasts truth brought to them with their own falsehood, reversing their accusation.
It forbids remaining with those who disbelieve in and ridicule God's verses and joins them to Hell.
A proof and clear light have come from the Lord, supplying the positive form of truth's arrival.
Disbelief joined to blocking God's way and wrongdoing brings painful punishment, a broad public consequence.
The unsupported claim to future wealth and children is too indirect to add to the focus.
Blocking the Sacred Mosque while falsely claiming guardianship supports the focus's disbelief-and-punishment horizon.
The plotters' scheme rebounds on the disbelievers, a general reversal rather than a direct truth relation.
It makes disbelief socially consequential by coupling it with blocking others from God's path.
Their demand for punishment if the message is truth illustrates a self-sealing refusal to receive it.
Pilgrimage procedures do not clarify the focus's accusation, denial, or final abode.
It names the true word about Jesus amid dispute, countering fabricated claims about God.
It explicitly exposes people fabricating lies against Allah and calls that alone a manifest sin.
It treats return to false worship as fabrication of a lie against Allah, clarifying the allegiance implied by such false speech.
It challenges those who declare divine provision lawful or forbidden without warrant, asking whether they fabricate against Allah.
It states directly that those who fabricate lies against Allah will not prosper, matching the focus's moral verdict.
It shows people attributing to Allah what they themselves reject while their tongues assert falsehood.
It identifies fabrication of lies with disbelief in Allah's signs and calls its practitioners the liars.
It forbids declaring things lawful or forbidden by false speech, since fabricating against Allah cannot succeed.
It asks who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah, a direct formulation of the focus's opening judgment.
A confirming Book comes to them, yet they disbelieve in it, providing a clear arrival-and-rejection pattern.
When a messenger confirms what they possess, some cast Allah's Book behind them, showing rejection after revelation arrives.
Earlier communities receive messengers with clear proofs yet declare disbelief in what they were sent with.
After every sign is shown to Pharaoh, he denies and refuses, a concise sign-arrival analogue to the focus.
They reject the signs unjustly and arrogantly despite inward certainty, intensifying the focus's account of culpable denial.
The revelation is described as clear verses, and only wrongdoers deny Allah's signs, framing the truth refused in the focus.
Those who defiantly disbelieve are returned to the Fire whenever they seek escape, developing Hell as enforced residence.
For disbelievers, Hell contains an enduring punishment without death or relief, expanding the focus's abode consequence.
Disbelievers are driven to Hell in groups after its gates open, giving narrative form to the focus's final destination.
Those who deny the Book and the message borne by messengers are told they will come to know the consequence.
It names the Fire as the enemies of Allah's recompense for denying His signs.
When truth comes to them, they call it magic and openly disbelieve, closely matching the focus's denial upon arrival.
The fabrication charge against the messenger is met with a challenge to produce comparable discourse, testing that accusation.
When Jesus brings clear proofs, they label them manifest magic, a direct pattern of rejecting arrived truth.
The message is relabeled inherited magic, showing a dismissive false classification of disclosed truth.
When Allah's verses are recited, they are dismissed as tales of the ancients, a recurrent mode of truth-denial.
